Subject: RFI: throughput targets and GPU-family question for Dedicated reservation

Markus,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. The procurement RFI has a section asking for a concise description of how Redwood maps reservation tiers to GPU families and what tradeoffs we should expect for our inferred workloads. They also want example throughput numbers for the following workload profiles: short-chat (avg 60 tokens, 95th latency <150ms), long-form summarization (avg 800 tokens, throughput target 20 reqs/min), and vector embedding heavy (batch embed 64 at a time).

Can you provide:
- a clear matrix that maps A100/H100/L4 style SKUs to expected tokens/sec and per-token cost at 8k context;
- guidance on how quantization (Q4/Q8) will affect tail latency and model capacity;
- recommended reservation sizing scenarios tied to 95th pct SLOs and fallbacks if peak bursts exceed reserved throughput (e.g., burst lanes, on-demand fallback).

The buyer wants this in a single-threaded response that we can include in the RFP packet by EOD Friday (their legal and infra teams read it closely). If you need detail about their traffic pattern I'll forward the anonymized histogram.

Attachments: none in this message.

Samantha Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Procurements Ltd.
From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: RFI: throughput targets and GPU-family question for Dedicated reservation

Samantha —

Thanks, good prompts. I put together a concise response and attached our GPU-fitment workbook (redwood_gpu_fitment_v3.xlsx) plus a CSV with three reservation scenarios (commitment_scenarios_20280415.csv). High level summary below — please feel free to drop these straight into the RFP packet.

Executive summary (short):
- H100-class: best for high-throughput long-context models (8k+), lowest latency at scale for generation workloads, higher unit cost but better density for batching long-form.
- A100-class: good middle ground for mixed workloads (chat + mid-length generation). Strong in quantized 8-bit modes; cost-effective for steady-state throughput.
- L4-class (or inference-optimized accelerators): lowest cost per embedding and short-chat inference; excellent for tiny-context or high-concurrency low-latency calls. Not suitable for sustained long-context generation at high tokens/sec.

Throughput examples (8k context, illustrative):
- Short-chat (60 tokens avg, per-request generation ~120 tokens produced):
  - H100: ~1,400–1,800 tokens/sec per GPU (low-tail latency with batching);
  - A100: ~900–1,200 tokens/sec per GPU;
  - L4: ~250–450 tokens/sec (optimized for small outputs);
- Long-form summarization (800 tokens avg request, 800 tokens produced):
  - H100: ~500–700 tokens/sec per GPU (better batching efficiency on long sequences);
  - A100: ~300–450 tokens/sec;
  - L4: not recommended (memory and kernel fit limits);
- Embeddings (batch size 64, 1536-d model):
  - L4: ~1,200–1,800 vectors/sec per card;
  - A100: ~2,500–3,500 vectors/sec;
  - H100: ~3,500–5,000 vectors/sec (depending on quantization and memory layout).

Quantization impact: Q4 (4-bit) typically reduces memory footprint and can increase packing density by ~2x versus fp16, improving tokens/sec for high-concurrency workloads. Q8 preserves more fidelity but gives smaller density gains. For long-context generation, Q4 may slightly increase tail latency variability due to lower-precision kernel fallbacks; we recommend validating with a small eval set. Our Optimize tool produces recommended quant profiles by workload (included in the workbook).

Reservation sizing guidelines (3 scenarios attached in CSV):
- Conservative (SLA-forward): provision based on 95th percentile sustained traffic * 1.15 buffer. Use H100 primary with A100 overflow. Include a reserved burst lane of 15% capacity to accommodate traffic spikes; configure on-demand fallback to hosted instances when burst > reserved.
- Balanced (cost/perf): A100 primary for mixed workloads, tier L4 pools for embeddings. Reserve enough to cover 80th–90th sustained throughput and rely on short on-demand bursts.
- Cost-min (embedding-heavy): L4 primary with small A100 pool for long-form fallbacks. Reserve at 70% of long-term median.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- Model variants pinned per route: prefer quantized/faster variants when tail latency grows.
- Automated routing: route non-critical traffic to lower-cost pools during overload; preserve critical SLO traffic on H100 lanes.
- Circuit breaker: when tail latency exceeds threshold, temporarily reduce beam size and degrade to faster model.

Attachments: redwood_gpu_fitment_v3.xlsx (workbook with measured p99/p95 numbers from internal benchmarks), commitment_scenarios_20280415.csv (three sizing scenarios), latency_throughput_matrix.png (visual).

Irene — can you add the kernel-fit caveats for L4s (memory mapping limits) and a sentence on operational burst policy? Jonas — please double-check the tokens/sec numbers I pulled from the 3/2028 benchmark set — I rounded to make the RFP readable.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Markus / Samantha —

Quick additions and a small correction to Markus's numbers after validating with kernel telemetry:
- L4 kernel fit: some transformer architectures with >12K internal kv cache references will hit memory fragmentation on L4-class boards when quantized to Q4; recommend L4 only for <=8k sequence/short outputs.
- A100 quantized tokens/sec improves further when memory is configured with contiguous KV caching; plan for +10% tokens/sec in that case.
- For embedding pipelines: if you have synchronous embedding calls embedded in user-facing flows, keep a small warm pool of L4 cards to maintain 95th latency <120ms.

Operational playbook (short bullets to drop into RFP):
- Reservation: commit to a monthly reserved pool per region; configure autoscale buffer of +10–20% based on historical burst patterns.
- Burst handling: reserved burst lane (pre-warmed) for up to 20% sustained bursts for up to 10 minutes; beyond that we failover to on-demand hosted capacity with automatic routing and spend alerting.
- Rollout safety: canary 5–10% traffic and automated rollback based on latency/regression signals.

I also attached the latency_throughput_matrix.png with p50/p95/p99 lines per GPU for their reference.

Jonas — I included a short note in the matrix about kernel selection when serving multi-model tenants; happy to expand if you think the buyer will need it.

Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Performance
Redwood Inference
